A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CompressTracker and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations and appendices. Corresponding material can be matched despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original tracker-compression experiments, benchmark results and ablations in Sections 4 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and reports additional compressed trackers, scalability experiments and CPU measurements in Tables 1–2.

M1.justification: Stage division, Bernoulli replacement, progressive replacement, prediction guidance, feature mimicking and inference remain unchanged. All three appendix pseudocode listings are identical apart from formatting. Additional tracker configurations do not introduce a documented procedural adaptation.

E1.justification: Both versions train on LaSOT, TrackingNet, GOT-10K and COCO and evaluate on LaSOT, LaSOText, TNL2K, TrackingNet and UAV123. Added teacher architectures and resolution configurations retain the same tracking task and dataset coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 adds SUTrack-T to the efficient-tracker comparison while retaining the previous external comparators. Its new Table 10 presents a dedicated distillation/pruning comparison using methods already represented in v1. The MixFormerV2 and SMAT comparator sets are preserved.

E3.justification: v2 adds SeqTrack, ODTrack and SUTrack configurations, larger-teacher and higher-resolution experiments, and CPU timing. Section 4.1 also changes the stated search-image resolution from 288×288 to 256×256 while retaining the principal training budget and optimizer settings. This establishes a reported setting revision, not that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 and Table 2 substantially extend generalization testing across teacher families and introduce explicit tests of teacher scale and resolution. Existing initialization, stage-division, supervision, replacement-probability and progressive-replacement analyses remain; their relocation does not constitute new analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without seed information, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting procedure is added.

E6.justification: v2 adds five-benchmark results for compressed SeqTrack, ODTrack and SUTrack, with LaSOT AUCs of 68.1, 70.5 and 72.2, respectively, plus larger-teacher, higher-resolution and CPU-speed results. The original OSTrack sweep, MixFormerV2/SMAT tables and existing ablation values are retained. The additions concern different configurations, not demonstrated same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v2 Equations 1–4 formalize stage organization and replacement already described in v1. Its progressive-replacement equation is algebraically equivalent to v1 Equation 1; the expectation expression and total loss are unchanged. No new theorem, proof or substantive mathematical assumption appears.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list shift the headline performance claim from CompressTracker-4 retaining approximately 96% accuracy with 2.17× acceleration of OSTrack to CompressTracker-SUTrack retaining approximately 99% with 2.42× acceleration. The central claims of general, structurally flexible compression and simplified training remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds an explanation relating the performance of retained variants to layer count and MLP width in Appendix 6.1. It removes v1's explicit residual-performance-gap limitation and surveillance-misuse discussion. Training-overhead qualifications remain in the training-time discussion and Appendix 6.2.

D1.justification: v2 identifies the CPU timing hardware as an Intel Xeon Platinum 8268 at 2.90 GHz and revises the documented search-image size. Existing optimizer settings, loss weights, training budgets, GPU information, pseudocode and code-repository access are substantially retained; the new tracker configurations receive limited individual implementation detail.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including SUTrack, ODTrack, DeTrack and Progressive Scaling Visual Object Tracking, while removing works including SiamBAN, InstructSeq and OneVOS. The basic positioning against lightweight architecture design and MixFormerV2's compression strategy remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are rewritten, Section 3.5 adds an explanation of component connections, and the experimental narrative is reorganized around compression and generalization. Heterogeneous-model experiments move to the appendix, several appendix ablations move into the main text, and the dedicated limitations and broader-impact sections disappear.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout throughout. Benchmark tables are consolidated and reorganized, CPU columns and a compression-technique comparison table are added, and multiple tables and plots move between the main text and appendix. The five existing figures retain their substantive visual content.

improvement.justification: The additional teacher-family, scale and resolution experiments strengthen evidence for the framework's claimed generality, while CPU measurements make its efficiency claims more practically assessable. Earlier experimental evidence is retained. These gains are moderated by sparse configuration-specific details and removal of explicit performance-gap and misuse qualifications; they support a limited overall improvement rather than a demonstrated methodological advance.
